content:
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

ui <- dashboardPage(
  dashboardHeader(
    title = "WFE – Practicals",
    titleWidth = 300
  ),
  
  dashboardSidebar(
    width = 300,
    sidebarMenu(
      id = "practicals",
      menuItem("Welcome", tabName = "welcome", icon = icon("home")),
      menuItem("Practical 1: Gradients", tabName = "prac1", icon = icon("mountain"),
               menuSubItem("Step 1.1 – What is a gradient?", tabName = "p1_step1"),
               menuSubItem("Step 1.2 – Geospatial parameters", tabName = "p1_step2"),
               menuSubItem("Step 1.3 – Setup & transect", tabName = "p1_step3"),
               menuSubItem("Step 1.4 – Loading Climate", tabName = "p1_step4"),
               menuSubItem("Step 1.5 – Extracting values", tabName = "p1_step5"),
               menuSubItem("Step 1.6 – Plotting the transect", tabName = "p1_step6"),
               menuSubItem("Step 1.7 – Which biome?", tabName = "p1_step7"),
               menuSubItem("Step 1.8 – Biomes", tabName = "p1_step8"),
               menuSubItem("Step 1.9 – Wrap-up", tabName = "p1_step9")
      ),
      menuItem("Practical 2: Crop production", tabName = "prac2", icon = icon("sun-plant-wilt"),
               menuSubItem("Step 2.1 – Water stress and yield",tabName = "p2_step1"),
               menuSubItem("Step 2.2 – A hypothetical growing season",tabName = "p2_step2"),
               menuSubItem("Step 2.3 – Amsterdam baseline climate", tabName = "p2_step3" ),
               menuSubItem("Step 2.4 – Future climate scenarios",tabName = "p2_step4" ),
               menuSubItem("Step 2.5 – Compare scenarios",tabName = "p2_step5"),
               menuSubItem("Step 2.6 – Interpretation and limitations", tabName = "p2_step6")
      ),
      menuItem("Practical 3: Biodiversity", tabName = "prac3", icon = icon("kiwi-bird"),
               menuSubItem("Step 3.1 – Camera traps", tabName = "p3_step1"),
               menuSubItem("Step 3.2 – Environmental extraction", tabName = "p3_step2"),
               menuSubItem("Step 3.3 – Relationships", tabName = "p3_step3")
      ),
      menuItem("Practical 4: Geodiversity", tabName = "prac4", icon = icon("globe"),
               menuSubItem("Step 4.1 – Global layers", tabName = "p4_step1"),
               menuSubItem("Step 4.2 – Sampling", tabName = "p4_step2"),
               menuSubItem("Step 4.3 – Models", tabName = "p4_step3")
      ),
      menuItem("Practical 5: Crop Suitability", tabName = "prac5", icon = icon("seedling"),
               menuSubItem("Step 5.1 – Load data", tabName = "p5_step1"),
               menuSubItem("Step 5.2 – Suitability function", tabName = "p5_step2"),
               menuSubItem("Step 5.3 – Climate scenarios", tabName = "p5_step3")
      ),
      menuItem("Practical 6: Crop Diversity", tabName = "prac6", icon = icon("wheat-awn"),
               menuSubItem("Step 6.1 – Crop area & richness", tabName = "p6_step1"),
               menuSubItem("Step 6.2 – Diversity & vulnerability", tabName = "p6_step2")
      )
    )
  ),
  
  dashboardBody(
    tags$head(
      tags$style(HTML("
        .recap {
          background-color: #98F5FF;
          border-left: 4px solid #1d6b99;
          padding: 10px;
          margin-bottom: 15px;
        }
        .todo {
          background-color: #FFFFCC;
          border-left: 4px solid #1d6b99;
          padding: 10px;
          margin-bottom: 15px;
        }
        .recap_geospatial {
          background-color: #7FFFd4;
          border-left: 4px solid #1d6b99;
          padding: 10px;
          margin-bottom: 15px;
        }
        .recap_theory {
          background-color: #FFFACD;
          border-left: 4px solid #1d6b99;
          padding: 10px;
          margin-bottom: 15px;
        }
        .question {
          background-color: #fff9e6;
          border-left: 4px solid #e6a700;
          padding: 10px;
          margin-bottom: 15px;
        }
        .reflection {
          background-color: #f5f5f5;
          border-left: 4px solid #777;
          padding: 10px;
          margin-bottom: 15px;
        }

        code {
          background-color: #f2f2f2;
          padding: 1px 3px;
          border-radius: 3px;
        }
        pre.code-block {
          background-color: #f7f7f7;
          border: 1px solid #ddd;
          padding: 10px;
          overflow-x: auto;
          font-family: 'Source Code Pro', monospace;
          font-size: 0.9em;
          margin-bottom: 15px;
        }
      "))
    ),
    
    tabItems(
      # ========== WELCOME ==========
      tabItem(
        tabName = "welcome",
        fluidPage(
          h2("Welcome to World Food & Ecosystems – R Practicals"),
          p(
            "This Shiny app guides you through six R-based practicals using local spatial data.",
            " Each practical has multiple steps accessible from the left sidebar menu."
          ),
          tags$div(
            class = "recap",
            strong("How to use this app:"), tags$br(),
            tags$ol(
              tags$li("Select a practical from the left sidebar (Practical 1–6)."),
              tags$li("Navigate through steps within each practical."),
              tags$li("Read explanations, questions, and code examples."),
              tags$li("Write and run code in your own R script or RMarkdown document."),
              tags$li("Do NOT copy-paste code; type it yourself to learn.")
            )
          ),
          tags$div(
            class = "question",
            strong("Important:"), tags$br(),
            "The goal is to practice writing R code. Use the code examples as templates,",
            " but adapt them to your own data and variable names. "
          ),
          h3("Practicals overview"),
          tags$ul(
            tags$li("Practical 1: Gradients and patterns – transect sampling and visualization"),
            tags$li("Practical 2: Crop growth, yields and water stress"),
            tags$li("Practical 3: Biodiversity from Camera Traps – richness vs environment"),
            tags$li("Practical 4: Geodiversity and Global Biodiversity – global raster analysis"),
            tags$li("Practical 5: Crop Suitability Modelling – rule-based suitability maps"),
            tags$li("Practical 6: Global Crop Diversity – agricultural richness and vulnerability")
          )
        )
      ),
      
      # ========== PRACTICAL 1 ==========
      tabItem(
        tabName = "p1_step1",
        fluidPage(
          h2("Practical 1, Step 1 – What is a gradient?, how can environmental data be leveraged to understand a pattern"),
          p(
            "Gradient analysis examines how variables change along a spatial or environmental gradient.",
            " In this practical, we look at a West–East transect in Oregon, USA, and study how elevation,",
            " temperature and precipitation change along that line. We will also look at the occurrence of blueberry fields and investigate in which conditions they thrive"
          ),
          p(
            "Research Question 1: how does precipitation and temperature change along a W-E gradient in the Willamette valley (US)",
            "Research Question 2: What does this imply for the biome classification of the region ",
            "Research Question 3: where does blueberry production occur and to which extent can the spatial pattern be explained by T and P regimes"
          ),
          tags$div(
            class = "recap_geospatial",
            strong("From a geo-spatial perspective"), tags$br(),
            "A transect analysis is when you overlay a line (vector file) with raster files and extract the values of the raster file along the line/transect",tags$br(),
            "Next to the transect analysis we will extract the raster values for precipitation, temperature and elevation for blueberry fields, which are represented by points"
          ),
          tags$div(
            class = "recap_theory",
            strong("Connection to the theory"), tags$br(),
            "Today in class, we saw the importance of understanding patterns to better grasp how biomes/climate/food production interlink. Today in the practical course we will tackle a concrete example of a sharply changing environment and the agricultural production that is possible in certain niche locations"

          )
        )
      ),
      
      tabItem(
        tabName = "p1_step2",
        fluidPage(
          h2("Practical 1, Step 2 – Geospatial variables"),
          p(
            "Before analyzing data, we need to define the geospatial characteristics of the study: extent, resolution,",
            " dimensions (processes), and the working hypothesis. Subsequently, we need to find and download the data"
          ),
          tags$table(
            class = "table table-striped",
            tags$thead(
              tags$tr(
                tags$th("Variable"),
                tags$th("Description")
              )
            ),
            tags$tbody(
              tags$tr(tags$td("Spatial extent"), tags$td("North-West USA (transect in Oregon)"),
              tags$tr(tags$td("Cartographic unit"), tags$td("Transect (line)")),
              tags$tr(tags$td("Dimensions"), tags$td("Elevation, temperature, precipitation")),
              tags$tr(tags$td("Dimension sources"), tags$td("Copernicus DEM, WorldClim")),
              tags$tr(tags$td("Temporal resolution"), tags$td("> 30-year climate averages")),
              tags$tr(tags$td("Spatial resolution"), tags$td("DEM = 90m, WorldClim = ca. 1km"))
              )
            )
          ),
          tags$div(
            class = "reflection",
            strong("Reflection: forming the hypothesis"), tags$br(),
            "Read the paper by Giombolini et al. 2011: In the paper, the authors describe the Willamette valley to be bounded between the Cascade and Coastal mountain ranges. Do you think it will be hotter/colder and drier/wetter on the east and west of the valley?"
          ),
          tags$div(
            class = "question",
            strong("Quiz question 1"), tags$br(),
            "Read the paper by Giombolini et al. 2011: The soil types described are not part of the WRB classification, based their description of the USDA soil classification, which WRB equivalent soils DO NOT occur in the Willamette valley?"
          )
        )
      ),
      
      tabItem(
        tabName = "p1_step3",
        fluidPage(
          h2("Practical 1, Step 3 – Setup & transect"),
          p(
            "Now we start the analysis, this means we need to first install (with the command install.packages()) and load (with the command library() the following packages:."
          ),
          h3("3.1 Load packages"),
          p("In your own script, load the following packages (install them first if needed):"),
          tags$ul(
            tags$li("devtools"),
            tags$li("rlang"),
            tags$li("geodata"),
            tags$li("ggplot2"),
            tags$li("plotbiomes"),
            tags$li("terra")
          ),
          tags$div(
            "Example of how this might look in your script:",
            tags$pre(class = "code-block",
                     "install.packages(c(\"terra\"))  # if you still need to install the package
library(terra)") #to load the package
          ),
          p("Repeat this for all the packages listed above that are required."),
          tags$br(),
          p("We will also use one custom made package that we will install from github to plot biomes"),
          tags$div(
            "This is how you do that:",
            tags$pre(class = "code-block",
                     "devtools::install_github('valentinitnelav/plotbiomes')")),
          h3("3.2 Download the digital elevation model and load it into R"),
          tags$div(
            class = "todo",
            strong("Task"), tags$br(),
            "You will need to download the digital elevation model for the region. 
            You need to browse to this website: https://portal.opentopography.org/raster?opentopoID=OTSDEM.032021.4326.1.
            How to do download the DEM is shown here:",
            tags$video(
              controls = TRUE,
              width = "100%",
              style = "max-width: 900px;",
              tags$source(
                src = "downloaddemsmall.mp4",
                type = "video/mp4"
              ),
              "Your browser does not support the video tag."
            ),
            "Now extract and store the file in your working directory, and subsequently load this rasterfile into your R environment: "
          ),
          tags$pre(class = "code-block",
                   "# Example pattern (edit paths to match your own files):
elevation   <- rast('C:/PeterSelie/WFEpracticals/naamvandem.tif')
elevation   # print basic info to the console
#now you can even plot the dem:
plot(elevation)")
          ,
          h3("3.3 Define the transect line"),
          tags$div(
            "Define a West–East transect in Oregon",
            tags$ul(
              tags$li("Start (West): longitude -124, latitude 44.8"),
              tags$li("End (East): longitude -121.3, latitude 44.8")
            ),
            "We will make a transect between these two points, and make it as such that the transect consists of 100 points"
          ),
          tags$pre(class = "code-block",
                   "# Example pattern for the transect:
north_latitude <- 44.8
south_latitude<- 44.8
west_longitude <- -124
east_longitude <- -121.3
n_points<-100

# Longitudes at 0.01-degree intervals
longitude <- seq(
  from = west_longitude,
  to = east_longitude,
  length.out = n_points)
# Latitudes at 0.01-degree intervals
latitude <- seq(
  from = north_latitude,
  to = south_latitude,
  length.out = n_points)
transect <- data.frame(
  lon = longitude,
  lat = rep(latitude, n_points)
)
View(transect)
coordinates <- as.matrix(transect[, c('lon', 'lat')])
#you can now even add the transect to your plot: 
points(transect, col = 'black', pch = 16, cex = 0.7)
                   ")
          ,
        tags$div(
          class = "reflection",
          strong("reflection" ), tags$br(),
          "What would you need to change in order to have the transect run from north to south of the Netherlands?"
        ),
          tags$div(
            class = "question",
            strong("Quiz question 2"), tags$br(),
            "Give this plot an appropriate title, and include your student number in the titel. Change the color of the transect to one of your choice"
          )
        )
      ),
      
      tabItem(
        tabName = "p1_step4",
        fluidPage(
          h2("Practical 1, Step 4 – Loading Temperature and Precipitation from worldclim"),
          p(
            "We will now extract the elevation values, precipitation values and temperature values along the points of the transect.",
            " For the elevation, we can use the DEM (Digital Elevantion Model). For the precipitation and temperature, we can use the geodata package you installed and loaded before - which contains all the WorldClim data. WorldClim is a global initiative that hosts long term average and mothly data for each ca 1x1km2 grid worldwide.",
            " The worldclim command we will use will download the data for a specific tile (section on earth). Let's first understand what we need to provide to the command in order to get the data we want:"
          ),
          tags$pre(class = "code-block",
                   "# we want to use the command worldclim_tile, but we don't really know how it works, so let's check it out:
?worldclim_tile")
          ,
          p("Great, now we know we need to provide a longitude and latitude, and the variable of interest (in our case this is prec and tavg, short for precipitation and average temperature)"),
          p("We are providing you with the code to extract precipitation, please complete the code below to also extract the average temperature"),
          tags$pre(class = "code-block",
                   "# let's get our data:
us_prec <- worldclim_tile(
  lon = -122,
  lat = 44.8,
  var = 'prec',
  path = tempdir()
)
us_tavg<-????????
                   "),
        p("the tiles are way bigger than the Willamette valley extent, so we can crop them to get a smaller extent. This is how you do that:"),
        tags$pre(class = "code-block",
                 "# first define the Willamette valley extent::
willamette_extent <- ext(
  -124,    # xmin: western longitude
  -121.3,  # xmax: eastern longitude
  44,    # ymin
  45     # ymax
)
#now you can crop the temperature and precipitation layers:
willamette_tavg <- crop(us_tavg, willamette_extent)
willamette_prec <-crop(us_prec, willamette_extent)
     "),
    
    tags$br(),
    tags$br(),
    
    p("Now let's plot and inpsect these temperature and precipitation layers:"),
    tags$pre(class = "code-block",
             "# plot the precipitation layer and the temperature layer: :
plot(willamette_tavg)
plot(willamette_prec)
     "), 
    p("These are monthly values, but we actually want a yearly value. For the precipitation, it makes sense to sum all the monthly values to get the total amount of rainfall. However, for the temperature, this does not make sense: instead of using the sum, how would you aggregate the information for all the months into one number? "), 
    tags$pre(class = "code-block",
             "# take the mean temperature and the sum of the precipitation. This is done through the app function, let's also explore what it does first:
?app
temp_average_willamette <- app(willamette_tavg, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
prec_average_willamette <- app(willamette_prec, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
#let's now plot it again:
plot(temp_average_willamette)
plot(prec_average_willamette)
             "),
    p("The temperature map looks good, but the precipitation map has a bit a weird colour set: we want yellow to be dry and blue to be wet:"),
    tags$pre(class = "code-block",
             "#try to adjust the colours of the precipitation : 
dry_to_wet <- colorRampPalette(
  c(
    '#FEE08B',  # yellow: very dry
             '#FDAE61',  # light orange
             '#F46D43',  # orange
             '#74ADD1',  # light blue
             '#2C7BB6'   # dark blue: very wet
    )
        )(100)
  
  plot(prec_average_willamette, col = dry_to_wet)
             ")
        )
      ),
      
      tabItem(
        tabName = "p1_step5",
        fluidPage(
          h2("Practical 1, Step 5 – Elevation profile"),
          p(
            "Now extract elevation along the transect using the DEM and plot it as a function of longitude."
          ),
          p("We do this with the function 'extract' from the terra package. First inspect how it works, then execute this."),
          p("The example for the elevation is given, complete this for precipitation and temperature"),
          tags$pre(class = "code-block",
                   "# Example extraction:
#extract values of elevation for the transect, we call the outcome demWV (the dem values for our transect in Willamette Valley)
demWV <- terra::extract(elevation, coordinates)
temperatureWV <- ???
precWV <- ???

#now let's bundle this all together into one dataframe:
matrix_WV<-as.data.frame(cbind(demWV,temperatureWV,precWV))
colnames(matrix_WV)<-c('elevation', 'temperature', 'precipitation')

#now inpsect your dataframe: does it look okay?
View(matrix_WV)
                   ")
        )
      ),
      
      tabItem(
        tabName = "p1_step6",
        fluidPage(
          h2("Practical 1, Step 6 – Plotting the transect"),
          p(
            "Now we are finally ready to plot the temperature and the precipitation along the longitudes",
            "For this we use ggplot, a sophisticated way of plotting data in R.",
            "To understand what ggplot can do please check https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/articles/ggplot2.html. ",
            "In the code below we also comment the ggplot command so that you understand what each line does. ",
            "Below we give the example for temperature, repeat this for precipitation"
          ),
          tags$pre(class = "code-block",
                   "
ggplot(matrix_WV, aes(x = longitude, y = temperature)) + #in this line we say to ggplot which data we want to plot, and which parts of the data should be considered the x and y
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, colour = 'orange')  #in this line, we say that we want to plot a line (not points) and we identify the line width and the colour
                   "),
          tags$div(
            class = "question",
            strong("Quiz question 3"), tags$br(),
            "Make the same plot for precipitation, give the line a blue colour, provide a unit to the y-axis and add your student number to the title."
          )

          

        )
      ),
      
      tabItem(
        tabName = "p1_step7",
        fluidPage(
          h2("Practical 1, Step 7 – Which biome?"),
          p(
            "In this section we will plot the Whitakker biome plot and check out where the Willamette valley is located",
            "The whitakker plot can be easily plotted by the custom package 'plotbiomes' we installed and loaded at the start of this practical."
          ),
          tags$div(
            class = "recap",
            strong("Summary "), tags$br(),
            "In your script, you will" ,
            tags$ol(
              tags$li("plot a generic whitakker biome plot"),
              tags$li("Plot the temperature and precipitation along the 100 transect points on this plot"),
              tags$li("Solve any unit conversion issues along the way")
            )
          ),
          tags$pre(class = "code-block",
                   "# first plot the whitakker base plot:
whittaker_base_plot<-whittaker_base_plot()
whittaker_base_plot
#now add the points of the transect in Willamette valley
whittaker_base_plot +
  geom_point(data = matrix_WV, aes(x = temperature, y = precipitation), color = 'blue', size = 6)
")
          ,
          tags$div(
            class = "question",
            strong("Quiz question 4"), tags$br(),
            "There seems to be an issue with the precipitation values: solve this issue, give the plot your student number as a title and upload it to canvas"
          ),
          p(
            "Now the points encompass a transect ranging way beyond the Willamette valley itself (which extends from '-123.3' to '-122.8' longitude)",
            "Make a selection of the matrix_WV so that only these points are retained"
          ),
          tags$pre(class = "code-block",
                   "# Example selection:
                   #we first need to couple our coordinates explicitly to the matrix_WV
                   matrix_WV<-cbind(coordinates,matrix_WV)
                   #then we can make a selection
                  WV_only<-matrix_WV[which(matrix_WV$lon < -122.8 & matrix_WV$lon > -123.3),]


                      "),
          tags$div(
            class = "question",
            strong("Quiz question 5"), tags$br(),
            "Which biome is characterizing the valley itself?"
          ),
          tags$div(
            class = "reflection",
            strong("Reflection: is this biome suitable for blueberry production?"), tags$br(),
            "Check out the FAO data sheet for blueberries: https://ecocrop.apps.fao.org/ecocrop/srv/en/dataSheet?id=10714",
            "Based on the optimal and absolute temperatures and rainfall: is this biome suitable for blueberry production?"
          ),
          
        )
      ),
      
      tabItem(
        tabName = "p1_step8",
        fluidPage(
          h2("Practical 1, Step 8 – Blueberries"),
          p(
            "Now that we have a basic understanding of the geography along this Willamette transect,",
            "let's look at a specific crop"
          ),
          p("We will look at one of the most important fruit crops in this valley, the blueberry."),
          tags$div(
            class = "todo",
            strong("Task"), tags$br(),
            "You will need to download the shapefiles of blueberry fields in Willamette valley, this file is availble on canvas.",
            "Download the file, and extract the zip-file. Put it in your working directory and load it in R.",
            "The latter can be done with the function 'vect.' ",
            "We load the points (each representing a blueberry field) and plot them on the DEM map."
            
          ),
          tags$pre(class = "code-block",
                   "#load the shapefile
blueberries <- vect('C:/Users/AlainProvist/practica/blueberries_pointswgs.shp')
#plot the DEM
plot(elevation)
#add the points to the DEM:
plot(blueberries, add=TRUE, col='white')
                   )")
          ,
          p("Much like when we extracted the precipitation, temperature and DEM values along the transect, we can do the same now for the blueberry points"),
          p("complete the code below to extract the values"),
          tags$pre(class = "code-block",
                   "#extract the temperature and precipitation values for the blueberry fields
blueberrytemperature<-extract(temp_average_willamette, blueberries)
blueberryprec<-???
#now you can build a figure with two panels (left and right) showing the spread of temperature (left) and precipitation (right) of the blueberry fields
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
boxplot(blueberrytemperature)
boxplot(blueberryprec)

                   "),

          tags$div(
            class = "question",
            strong("Question 6"), tags$br(),
            "Based on the median of the average annual temperature and the median of the total precipitation for all the blueberry production points, and given the FAO ecocrop data sheet for blueberries (https://ecocrop.apps.fao.org/ecocrop/srv/en/dataSheet?id=10714) which statement is true:"
          )
        )
      ),

      
      tabItem(
        tabName = "p1_step9",
        fluidPage(
          h2("Practical 1, Step 9 – Wrap-up"),
          p(
            "You have now build a transect of precipitation, temperature and elevation along the Willamette valley",
            "together with an overview on in which temperature and precipitation niches the blueberry fields lie"
          ),
          tags$div(
            class = "recap",
            strong("Summary "), tags$br(),
            "As a recap, from a technical viewpoint, in this tutorial you have learned how to" ,
            tags$ol(
              tags$li("plot a generic whitakker biome plot"),
              tags$li("Load raster and vector files into R"),
              tags$li("Extract raster values for a collection of points"),
              tags$li("Visualize these transects and niches of growth"),
              tags$li("Solve any unit conversion issues along the way")
            )
          ),
          tags$div(
            class = "question",
            strong("Question 7"), tags$br(),
            "The Willamette valley is not fully covered in blueberries. They require a specific soil pH. Based on the blueberry data sheet by FAO, which WRB soil type (generally speaking, not constraint to Willamette valley) do you think is not suitable?"
          )
        )
      ),
# ========== PRACTICAL 2 ==========

tabItem(
  tabName = "p2_step1",
  fluidPage(
    h2("Practical 2, Step 1 – Water stress and crop yield"),
    tags$div(
      class = "recap",
      strong("Important to know before you start"), tags$br(),
      "In this practical a lot of code is given. It is not needed that you are able to reproduce all the code, but you are expected to understand what the various functions do and how to adjust them for e.g. a different climate/location or a different crop."
    ),
    p(
      "In this practical, you will estimate how water stress may affect maize yield near Amsterdam.",
      " You will first work with a hypothetical climate time series. You will then use WorldClim",
      " baseline climate data and CMIP6 future climate projections."
    ),
    
    tags$div(
      class = "recap_theory",
      strong("The central idea"), tags$br(),
      "A crop can only realise its maximum yield when its water demand is met. Reference",
      " evapotranspiration (ETo) describes atmospheric evaporative demand. Crop evapotranspiration",
      " under non-water-limiting conditions (ETm) depends on ETo and a crop coefficient (Kc).",

tabItem(
  tabName = "p2_step2",
  fluidPage(
    h2("Practical 2, Step 2 – A hypothetical growing season"),
    
    p(
      "Before downloading spatial climate data, we will calculate maize yield with a hypothetical",
      " monthly climate record. This allows you to understand each calculation before automating it."
    ),
    
    h3("2.1 Define location, crop properties, and monthly climate"),
    
    tags$pre(
      class = "code-block",
      "# Example location: Amsterdam\n",
      "longitude <- 4.90\n",
      "latitude <- 52.367\n\n",
      "# Maize is assumed to grow from May through August\n",
      "growing_months <- 5:8\n\n",
      "# Maximum attainable maize yield (tonnes per hectare)\n",
      "Ym <- 12\n\n",
      "# Hypothetical monthly climate data\n",
      "tmax_c <- c(6, 7, 10, 14, 18, 21, 23, 23, 19, 14, 9, 6)\n",
      "tmin_c <- c(1, 1, 3, 6, 9, 12, 14, 14, 11, 8, 4, 2)\n",
      "prec_mm <- c(80, 80, 80, 80, 80, 80, 80, 80, 80, 80, 80, 80)\n\n",
      "# Crop coefficients for May, June, July and August\n",
      "kc <- c(0.40, 0.75, 1.15, 0.85)\n\n",
      "# Yield-response factors for May, June, July and August\n",
      "ky <- c(0.40, 1.50, 0.50, 0.20)"
    ),
    
    h3("2.2 Calculate monthly reference evapotranspiration"),
    p(
      "The SPEI package includes the Hargreaves method. It estimates ETo from monthly minimum",
      " and maximum temperature, plus latitude. Latitude is needed because solar radiation varies",
      " geographically and seasonally."
    ),
    p(
      "The SPEI package requires the Tmin and Tmax to be defined s timeseries, so we do that first."
    ),
    
    tags$pre(
      class = "code-block",
      "tmax_ts <- ts(tmax_c, start = c(2026, 1), frequency = 12)\n", 
      "tmin_ts <- ts(tmin_c, start = c(2026, 1), frequency = 12)\n\n",
      "# ETo is in mm per month\n",
      "eto_hargreaves <- SPEI::hargreaves(\n",
      "  Tmin = tmin_ts,\n",
      "  Tmax = tmax_ts,\n",
      "  lat = latitude\n",
      ")\n\n",
      "print(eto_hargreaves)\n",
      "plot(eto_hargreaves,\n",
      "     ylab = 'Reference evapotranspiration (mm/month)',\n",
      "     main = 'Monthly reference evapotranspiration')"
    ),
    
    h3("2.3 Calculate crop water demand and water-limited yield"),
    
    tags$pre(
      class = "code-block",
      "# Keep May--August only\n",
      "eto_growing <- as.numeric(eto_hargreaves[growing_months])\n",
      "prec_growing <- prec_mm[growing_months]\n\n",
      "# Maximum crop evapotranspiration\n",
      "ETm <- kc * eto_growing\n\n",
      "# Simplified actual evapotranspiration:\n",
      "# The actual evapotranspiration is equal to the maximum ET or the rainfall - whichever is lowest\n",
      "ETa <- pmin(prec_growing, ETm)\n\n",
      "# Relative yield factor per crop-growth stage\n",
      "stage_yield_factor <- 1 - ky * (1 - ETa / ETm)\n",
      "stage_yield_factor <- pmax(0, pmin(stage_yield_factor, 1))\n\n",
      "# The most strongly affected stage constrains final yield\n",
      "relative_yield <- min(stage_yield_factor)\n",
      "Ya <- Ym * relative_yield\n",
      "yield_percent <- 100 * relative_yield\n\n",
      "Ya\n",
      "yield_percent"
    ),
    
    tags$div(
      class = "recap",
      strong("Interpretation"), tags$br(),
      "If precipitation is at least as high as ETm in every growth stage, ETa equals ETm and",
      " the water-limited yield equals Ym. When ETa is lower than ETm, water stress reduces yield.",
      " A larger Ky means that water stress in that stage has a greater effect on yield."
    ),
    
    tags$div(

    )
  )

      "  print(breaks)\n\n",
      "  # Assign values to classes 1 to 5\n",
      "  classified <- ifel(\n",
      "    raster_layer <= breaks[1], 1,\n",

      "      ifel(\n",

      "        ifel(raster_layer <= breaks[4], 4, 5)\n",
      "      )\n",
      "    )\n",
